severityScale.description: Weights are review-priority hints only. No rule, including a high-weight combination, authorizes automatic classification, blocking, or mailbox actions.

low.meaning: Supporting signal; never sufficient alone to block or classify.

medium.meaning: Review recommended when combined with at least one other independent signal.

high.meaning: Strong review signal when its required combination is fully met; still not automatic proof or an auto-block.

supportingSignals: sender local-part is seven random lowercase letters followed by a configured campaign marker
sender domain is an eight-letter random lowercase label, then a word label, then a rotating parent domain on a .biz, .biz.id, or .my.id public suffix
display name spoofs a well-known brand or support-team role, such as a Gmail support-team style label, that does not match the sender domain
health-spam lures such as stop-taking-drug claims for ED, blood-pressure, or prostate products, or a fake celebrity or television-network medical endorsement including Dr. Oz or CBS style claims
provider mailed-by or similar trust label such as Trusted Sender that does not match the sender domain
subscription-termination or Final Warning lure that includes a fabricated account identifier

rules.requiredCombination: At least one configured marker or exact parameter and one configured exact path in the same message. A configured host is a supporting infrastructure signal only; it is never sufficient alone and must not be used as a broad shared-cloud-provider block. Observed rotating parent domains and other supportingSignals are correlating context only and must not be used as domain blocks; a single message per rotating domain is insufficient for campaign.repeated-malicious-sender-domain.v1.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone.

senderAddressPatterns: local-part: seven random lowercase ASCII letters, then a dot, then a configured campaign marker such as 111.957097
domain: eight random lowercase ASCII letters, then a word label, then a rotating parent domain
supportingSignals: spoofed brand or support-team display name, including a Gmail support-team style label, that does not match the sender domain
health-spam lures including stop-taking-drug claims for ED, blood-pressure, or prostate products and fake Dr. Oz or CBS style medical claims
provider mailed-by or trust label such as Trusted Sender that does not match the sender domain
subscription-termination Final Warning lure with a fabricated account identifier

rules.requiredCombination: The sender address matches the configured local-part and rotating-domain pattern and contains a configured campaign marker. Supporting lure, display-name, and mailed-by signals raise review priority but are not required. Observed parent domains are examples of rotation only and must never be added as domain blocks from a single message per domain.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone. Do not promote observed rotating parent domains into campaign.repeated-malicious-sender-domain.v1 without repeated observations and a legitimate-counterexample review.

combinedClaims: account or subscription blocked or expired
threatened deletion of photos, videos, or cloud files
supportingSignals: brand claim mismatches the exact sender domain
rapidly rotating unrelated sender domains
repeated token structure across sender local parts

rules.requiredCombination: Multiple combined claims plus at least one supporting sender or infrastructure mismatch.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review; generic storage or renewal words are insufficient.

rules.requiredCombination: The exact sender registered domain matches a listed domain that had repeated campaign observations and no legitimate counterexample in reviewed mailboxes. Shared or public-infrastructure domains must never be listed here.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; listing a domain is not an automatic mailbox block.

rules.requiredCombination: Visible Authentication-Results or equivalent header reports SPF fail or softfail. A missing header is handled by a separate rule.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. An SPF failure alone must never block, classify, or be treated as proof of malice. Forwarding and mailing lists can produce SPF failures on legitimate mail.

rules.requiredCombination: Visible Authentication-Results or equivalent header reports DKIM fail or none.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. DKIM fail or none alone must never block or classify a message.

rules.requiredCombination: Visible Authentication-Results or equivalent header reports DMARC fail.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. A DMARC failure alone must never block or classify a message, though it may raise review priority when combined with independent identity or campaign signals.

headerConditions: Authentication-Results header missing when it is expected from the receiving path
ARC results missing, broken, or inconsistent with Authentication-Results
Conflicting authentication results across Authentication-Results and ARC sets

rules.requiredCombination: Authentication-Results or ARC data are missing when expected, or visible results are internally inconsistent.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. Missing or inconsistent auth headers alone must never block or classify a message. Some connectors do not expose these headers.

headerConditions: Return-Path registrable domain differs from the From registrable domain

rules.requiredCombination: The Return-Path or envelope-from registrable domain differs from the visible From registrable domain.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. Return-Path mismatch alone must never block or classify a message. Third-party senders and mailing lists commonly use a different Return-Path.

combinedClaims: sender or link domain is a lookalike, typo, or homoglyph of a well-known brand domain
the message claims that brand in the display name, logo, or visible text
supportingSignals: substituted or visually confusable characters in the domain or display text
added, dropped, or transposed characters relative to the genuine brand domain
unexpected country-code or extra public-suffix on a brand-like label

rules.requiredCombination: A lookalike, typo, or homoglyph domain plus an explicit claim of the corresponding well-known brand. A merely unusual domain without a brand claim is insufficient.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone.

combinedClaims: display name or visible branding impersonates a well-known organization
exact sender domain is a consumer freemail or similar shared mailbox provider

rules.requiredCombination: A well-known brand or official role is claimed in the display name or visible branding, and the exact sender domain is a shared freemail provider. Do not flag ordinary personal mail that does not claim an official brand role.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone.

domainPatterns: brand label appears to the left of a non-brand registrable domain, such as brand.com.evil.tld
brand label is joined with a security-looking token on an unrelated registrable domain, such as brand-login.tld

rules.requiredCombination: The sender or link hostname places a well-known brand label in a non-authoritative position or as a hyphenated lookalike on an unrelated registrable domain, and the message claims that brand.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone. Do not treat ordinary brand subdomains on the genuine registrable domain as this pattern.

headerConditions: Reply-To registrable domain differs from the From registrable domain

rules.requiredCombination: A Reply-To address is present and its registrable domain differs from the From registrable domain.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. A different Reply-To service alone must never block or classify a message, because legitimate outsourced or ticketing addresses are common.

combinedClaims: display name impersonates a well-known brand
display name contains hidden or ignorable formatting characters
exact sender domain does not belong to the claimed brand
supportingSignals: unexpected attachments with generic business-document names and a non-document octet-stream type
urgency around account, phone, or payment-detail changes
homoglyph or lookalike characters in visible body text
Cyrillic or other confusable homoglyphs in the display name
message preview or body padded with invisible characters
lure that a phone-number or account-detail update request was submitted or is pending review

rules.requiredCombination: Brand impersonation in the display name plus hidden or ignorable characters plus a sender-domain mismatch. Attachments, urgency claims, preview padding, and typographic homoglyphs are supporting only. Prefer this display-name or brand versus domain mismatch together with hidden-character signals over exact-address blocking, which can miss later messages in the same pattern.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone. Do not treat a message as phishing solely because of invisible-character or preview padding.
legitimateCounterexamples: Genuine billing or receipt mail from the stripe.com payment-processor domain, including receipts-plus or billing-plus local-part prefixes for a known merchant, must not be treated as phishing solely because of invisible-character or preview padding. Such padding is common in legitimate marketing and transactional mail.

combinedClaims: display name impersonates a well-known brand, including a crypto-exchange customer-assistance role
display name contains hidden, zero-width, or ignorable formatting characters, or Cyrillic or other confusable homoglyphs
exact sender domain is an unrelated organisational domain that does not belong to the claimed brand
supportingSignals: lure that a phone-number or account-detail update request was submitted or is pending review
small unexpected attachment
message preview or body padded with invisible characters
a previously blocked exact sender address later recurs, showing that per-address blocking is a weak control for this pattern

rules.requiredCombination: Brand or official-role impersonation in the display name, plus hidden or ignorable characters or typographic homoglyphs in the display name, plus a sender domain that does not belong to the claimed brand. Phone-update lures, small attachments, and invisible preview padding are supporting only. Listed organisational domains are examples of unrelated or likely-compromised senders, not a block list, because a compromised legitimate organisation may also send ordinary mail.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone. Prefer the display-name or brand versus domain mismatch together with hidden-character or homoglyph signals over exact-address blocking, which has been observed to miss later messages in the same pattern.
legitimateCounterexamples: Genuine billing or receipt mail from the stripe.com payment-processor domain, including receipts-plus or billing-plus local-part prefixes for a known merchant, must not be treated as phishing solely because of invisible-character or preview padding. Such padding is common in legitimate marketing and transactional mail.

combinedClaims: login, sign-in, or account verification lure
password reset, unlock, or credential-update lure
supportingSignals: brand or official-role claim mismatches the exact sender domain
destination link domain does not match the claimed brand
request to enter a password, one-time code, or recovery information off-session

rules.requiredCombination: At least one credential or verification lure plus at least one supporting sender or destination mismatch. Generic security wording without a lure and mismatch is insufficient.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone.

languagePatterns: immediate action required or final warning
account will be closed, locked, or suspended unless the recipient acts now
data, photos, or funds will be deleted or lost unless the recipient acts now

rules.requiredCombination: Urgency or threat language is present. This rule is supporting context only unless combined with an independent identity, authentication, campaign, or destination mismatch.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. Urgency wording alone must never block or classify a message, because legitimate notices can also be time-sensitive.

combinedClaims: unexpected invoice, payment, refund, or unpaid-balance claim
gift-card, prize, pallet, or survey-for-reward claim
supportingSignals: brand or official-role claim mismatches the exact sender domain
payment or prize link domain does not match the claimed brand or payment processor in a consistent way
request to pay by gift card, cryptocurrency, or an unusual prepaid method

rules.requiredCombination: A payment, invoice, refund, gift-card, or prize lure plus at least one supporting sender or destination mismatch. An ordinary expected receipt from a known processor is a counterexample.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone.

rules.requiredCombination: An unexpected HTML, archive, disk-image, executable, or macro-enabled attachment is present. Treat the type as a supporting signal; raise review priority when combined with a lure, brand mismatch, or campaign indicator. Expected archives from a known correspondent remain counterexamples.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone.

linkConditions: visible link text or displayed URL uses a different registrable domain than the actual href

rules.requiredCombination: A visible domain claim in link text or a displayed URL differs from the href registrable domain. Generic labels such as Click here make no domain claim and do not match this rule.
rules.verdictEffect: Send for review only; never classify or act from this rule alone. Some legitimate tracking links can also trigger this conservative signal.

linkConditions: URL uses a public shortener that hides the final destination
URL uses an open-redirect style path or parameter on an otherwise unrelated host

rules.requiredCombination: A public shortener or an open-redirect style URL is present. This is a supporting signal only and is not sufficient alone, because shorteners are also used in legitimate mail.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. A shortener or redirect alone must never block or classify a message.

hostClasses: shared object-storage or free web-hosting hostname
HTML page path hosted on shared storage or free hosting

rules.requiredCombination: A link points to an HTML page on shared object storage or free hosting. The shared host, including storage.googleapis.com, is never sufficient alone and must not be used as a broad provider block. Raise review priority only when combined with a configured campaign marker, exact path, brand mismatch, or credential or payment lure.
rules.verdictEffect: Supporting review signal only. A cloud or free-host HTML link alone must never block or classify a message.
